candidates.statement: We shall explore this link on a particular example of random matrices called *$\beta$-ensembles* or *$\beta$-log gases* [@Forrester], i.e. the probability distributions on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the density of the form $$p(x_1,\dots,x_n) = \frac{1}{Z} e^{V(x_1)+\cdots+V(x_n)} \prod_{i<j} |x_i - x_j|^{\beta},$$ where $V$ is some real-valued function and $Z$ is the normalization constant.

The class of random Young diagrams considered in the current paper as well as the classes from [@Moll2015; @BorodinGorinGuionnet2015] are of quite distinct flavors and it is not obvious why they should contain any elements in common, except for the trivial example given by the Jack--Plancherel measure.
candidates.section_title: Random Young diagrams related to log-gases

candidates.statement: For partitions $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_\ell$ we define their *cumulant* with respect to the character $\chi\colon \mathcal{P}\to\mathbb{R}$ as a coefficient in the expansion of the logarithm of an analogue of a multidimensional Laplace transform $$\label{eq:log-laplace} k^{\chi}_\ell(\pi_1,\dots,\pi_\ell):= \left. \frac{\partial^\ell}{\partial t_1 \cdots \partial t_\ell} \log \chi\left( e^{t_1 \pi_1+\cdots+t_\ell \pi_\ell} \right) \right|_{t_1=\cdots=t_\ell=0},$$ where the operations on the right-hand side should be understood in the sense of formal power series with coefficients either in $\mathbb{R}[\mathcal{P}]$ or in $\mathbb{R}$.
The above statement about the convergence of the random vector ${\Delta}_n$ should be understood in a rather specific sense, formulated with help of some suitable test functions.

As we shall see in [@DolegaSniady-examples-AFP], the distribution of the random Young diagram $\lambda_n$ can be equivalently formulated via [\[eq:proba-linearcomb-A\]](#eq:proba-linearcomb-A){reference-type="eqref" reference="eq:proba-linearcomb-A"} in terms of the corresponding natural reducible Jack character and [\[theo:lln\]](#theo:lln){reference-type="ref" reference="theo:lln"} as well as [\[theo:clt\]](#theo:clt){reference-type="ref" reference="theo:clt"} are applicable.
In order to speak about CLT one should consider a more refined scaling: the one in which one stretches the second Russian coordinate $v$ by a factor of $\sqrt{n}$.

For any tuple $x_1,\dots,x_\ell \in\mathcal{A}$ we define their *conditional cumulant* as $$\begin{gathered} \kappa_{\mathcal{A}}^{\mathcal{B}}(x_1,\dots,x_\ell) = [t_1 \cdots t_\ell] \log \mathbb{E}e^{t_1 x_1+\dots+t_\ell x_\ell} = \\ \left. \frac{\partial^\ell}{\partial t_1 \cdots \partial t_\ell} \log \mathbb{E}e^{t_1 x_1+\dots+t_\ell x_\ell} \right|_{t_1=\cdots=t_\ell=0} \in \mathcal{B}, \end{gathered}$$ where the operations on the right-hand side should be understood in the sense of formal power series in variables $t_1,\dots,t_\ell$.

Note that the cumulants for partitions which we introduced in [\[sec:concatenation\]](#sec:concatenation){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:concatenation"} fit into this general framework: for $\mathcal{A}:=\mathbb{R}[\mathcal{P}]$ one should take the semigroup algebra of partitions, for $\mathcal{B}:=\mathbb{R}$ the real numbers and for $\mathbb{E}:=\chi\colon\mathbb{R}[\mathcal{P}]\to\mathbb{R}$ the character.

candidates.statement: ::: lemma []{#lem:Sniady2006-recycled-zombie label="lem:Sniady2006-recycled-zombie"} Assume that $X\subseteq \mathscr{P}$ is a set with the property that each $z\in\mathscr{P}$ can be expressed as a polynomial in the elements of $X$: $$\label{eq:takie-jednomiany-lubie} z= \sum_{1\leq i \leq n} z_{i,1} \cdots z_{i,l_i}$$ for some $n\geq 0$ and $z_{i,j}\in X$ in such a way that such that for each value of $1\leq i\leq n$ $$\label{eq:lost-assumption} \deg z \geq \deg z_{i,1}+ \cdots +\deg z_{i,l_i};$$ in other words the degree of each monomial should be bounded from above by the degree of $z$.
In order to keep the notation light we shall make the dependence on $\alpha$ implicit and we shall simply write $\mathcal{S}_k(\lambda):=\mathcal{S}_k^{(\alpha)}(\lambda)$.
We shall discuss this issue in more detail in the remaining of this section as well as in \cref{sec:extra-terms-evil}.
